headline: 753 hospitalised in 24 hours as 3 more die of dengue
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in cases, with over 10,000 hospitalisations this month alone.
details: Three people died of dengue and 753 others were hospitalised across Bangladesh in a 24-hour period ending Tuesday morning, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The total death toll for the year has reached 74, with 20 of those deaths occurring within the current month.
A total of 25,601 people have been infected with dengue this year, with 10,291 of them hospitalised in August alone.
The surge in hospitalisations continues after significant numbers were recorded in previous months, including 9,206 in July and 2,907 in June.
caption:
3 more deaths and 753 new hospitalisations in just 24 hours. Dengue cases are surging across Bangladesh.

Three people died of dengue and 753 others were hospitalised across Bangladesh in a 24-hour period ending Tuesday morning, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The total death toll for the year has reached 74, with 20 of those deaths occurring within the current month.

A total of 25,601 people have been infected with dengue this year, with 10,291 of them hospitalised in August alone.

The surge in hospitalisations continues after significant numbers were recorded in previous months, including 9,206 in July and 2,907 in June.

headline_marked: Bangladesh to hold [[presidential election this Thursday]] after 35 years
headline: Bangladesh to hold presidential election this Thursday after 35 years
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Oli Ahmed will contest the vote as neither candidate withdrew their nomination.
details: For the first time in 35 years, Bangladesh will hold a presidential election. The vote is scheduled for this Thursday, August 20, as neither of the two contesting candidates withdrew their nominations by the Tuesday deadline.

The contest is between Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, representing the BNP, and Oli Ahmed, the candidate for the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance. The election will take place in the National Parliament chamber from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

The electorate consists of 349 Members of Parliament. While the BNP holds a two-thirds majority in the current parliament, the Jamaat alliance has 90 members. Due to Article 70 of the constitution, which prevents MPs from voting against their party's decision, Mirza Fakhrul's victory is considered highly likely.

Election Commission Secretary Akhtar Ahmed confirmed that ballot papers will be prepared today. The process involves MPs signing for their ballots, which will list candidates in alphabetical order, and casting their votes in designated boxes.
The move comes after the resignation of Md. Sahabuddin on July 24. According to the constitution, a new president must be elected within 90 days of a vacancy in the office.
caption:
A presidential election is happening this Thursday—the first time in 35 years that Bangladesh has not had a president elected unopposed.

For the first time in 35 years, Bangladesh will hold a presidential election. The vote is scheduled for this Thursday, August 20, as neither of the two contesting candidates withdrew their nominations by the Tuesday deadline.

The contest is between Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, representing the BNP, and Oli Ahmed, the candidate for the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance. The election will take place in the National Parliament chamber from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

The electorate consists of 349 Members of Parliament. While the BNP holds a two-thirds majority in the current parliament, the Jamaat alliance has 90 members. Due to Article 70 of the constitution, which prevents MPs from voting against their party's decision, Mirza Fakhrul's victory is considered highly likely.

Election Commission Secretary Akhtar Ahmed confirmed that ballot papers will be prepared today. The process involves MPs signing for their ballots, which will list candidates in alphabetical order, and casting their votes in designated boxes.

The move comes after the resignation of Md. Sahabuddin on July 24. According to the constitution, a new president must be elected within 90 days of a vacancy in the office.
